en: Dhritarashtra said: Sanjaya, my sons and the sons of Pandu gathered at Kurukshetra, the field of dharma, eager to fight. What did they do?
Sanjaya said: When King Duryodhana saw the Pandava army drawn up in battle order, he went to his teacher Drona and spoke these words.
"Teacher, look at this huge army of the sons of Pandu, arranged for battle by your own clever pupil, the son of Drupada."
"Here are brave men with great bows, equal to Bhima and Arjuna in war: Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, a great chariot-fighter."
"Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana and the strong king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best of men."
"Bold Yudhamanyu and strong Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra, and the sons of Draupadi, all of them great chariot-fighters."

first: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम ।
en: "Now hear, best of the twice-born, about the leading men on our side, the commanders of my army. I name them so that you know them."
"You yourself, Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa who wins in battle; Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadatta."

first: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।
en: "And many other heroes are ready to give their lives for me. They carry many kinds of weapons and are all skilled in war."
"Our army, guarded by Bhishma, cannot be measured, while their army, guarded by Bhima, is limited."
"So all of you, standing at your posts in every division, must protect Bhishma above all."
Then Bhishma, the old grandfather of the Kurus, roared like a lion and blew his conch loudly, to cheer Duryodhana.
Then conches, kettledrums, tabors, drums and horns all sounded at once, and the noise was tremendous.
Then Krishna and Arjuna, standing in their great chariot drawn by white horses, blew their divine conches.
Krishna blew Panchajanya, Arjuna blew Devadatta, and Bhima, the doer of fearsome deeds, blew his great conch Paundra.
King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
The king of Kashi, a great archer, Shikhandi the great chariot-fighter, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the unconquered Satyaki;
Drupada, the sons of Draupadi, and the strong-armed son of Subhadra, O lord of the earth, each blew his own conch.
That fierce sound, echoing through earth and sky, tore at the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons.
Then Arjuna, whose banner bears the monkey, saw Dhritarashtra's men standing ready. As weapons were about to clash, he lifted his bow.
O king, he then spoke these words to Krishna. Arjuna said: "Achyuta, place my chariot between the two armies,
so that I can look at those who stand here eager to fight, and see whom I must fight in this battle.
I want to see those who have gathered here to fight, wishing to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra."
Sanjaya said: O Bharata, when Arjuna spoke like this, Krishna placed that fine chariot between the two armies,
in front of Bhishma, Drona and all the kings, and said: "Arjuna, look at all these Kurus gathered here."
There Arjuna saw, standing in both armies, fathers and grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends,
fathers-in-law and well-wishers too. Seeing all these relatives standing there, Arjuna, son of Kunti,
was filled with deep pity and spoke in sorrow. Arjuna said: "Krishna, when I see my own people here, ready to fight,

first: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ।
en: my limbs grow weak and my mouth goes dry. My body trembles and my hair stands on end.
"My bow Gandiva slips from my hand and my skin burns. I cannot stand steady, and my mind seems to spin.
"Keshava, I see bad signs. I see no good in killing my own people in battle.

first: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च ।
en: "Krishna, I do not want victory, or a kingdom, or pleasures. What use is a kingdom to us, Govinda, or comforts, or even life?

first: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च ।
en: "The very people for whom we wanted a kingdom, pleasures and comforts stand here in battle, ready to give up their lives and wealth:
"teachers, fathers, sons, and grandfathers too; uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other relatives.
"Madhusudana, I do not want to kill them, even if they kill me, not even for rule over the three worlds, much less for this earth.
"Janardana, what joy can we have from killing the sons of Dhritarashtra? Only sin will come to us if we kill these attackers.
"So it is not right for us to kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our own relatives. How can we be happy, Madhava, after killing our own people?
"Even if they, with minds spoiled by greed, see no wrong in destroying a family and no sin in betraying friends,
"why should we not, who clearly see the evil of destroying a family, learn to turn away from this sin, Janardana?
"When a family is destroyed, its age-old traditions are lost. When tradition is lost, disorder takes over the whole family.
"Krishna, when disorder takes over, the women of the family go astray, and when the women go astray, the classes become mixed.
"This mixing leads to hell both the family and those who destroyed it. Their ancestors fall too, deprived of the offerings of food and water.
"Through these wrongs of the family-destroyers, which cause the mixing of classes, the lasting duties of caste and family are ruined.
"Janardana, we have heard that people whose family traditions are ruined must live in hell for a long time.

first: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् ।
en: "Alas, what a great sin we have set out to commit, ready to kill our own people out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom!
"It would be better for me if the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, killed me in battle while I stood unarmed and did not resist."
Sanjaya said: Having spoken like this on the battlefield, Arjuna put down his bow and arrows and sat down in the chariot, his mind overcome with grief.
